<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ac098549e0a16cf31c813380fa90a15156621635` — the merge of head `e57e7c05668dc6989a54f4ff616a6e5a0002498e` into base `d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ac098549e0a16cf31c813380fa90a15156621635 && git checkout ac098549e0a16cf31c813380fa90a15156621635
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433 e57e7c05668dc6989a54f4ff616a6e5a0002498e && git checkout -B drift-repro d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433 && git merge --no-ff e57e7c05668dc6989a54f4ff616a6e5a0002498e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e516f3534bd5f0d4eb74c140f8da53b2d4ec31ff`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.packageless-layered-read-refusal.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-layers-ambiguous-package.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-layers-ambiguous-package.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-qualified-item-read.test.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts (the plain read's `packagelessScopedRead`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-environment-rows.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, packages/rest/src/error-response.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-lock-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-catalog-echo.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, docs/adr/0150 (D3, D5), .changeset/32622-layers-two-holders-candidates.md (for ② only)

Inputs read: cards #32622 (body, 7 comments, the rework addendum 6897100983 included) and #32914 (body, 3 comments); PR #33885 body, file list (10 files) and the net diff against merge base `64807a9c`; the check-runs on the head, read at 2026-11-15T15:55Z. PR author login: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

Check-runs on the head as read (15:55Z): 25 completed success, among them Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Changeset (2), PR-body guards (2), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate (the aggregate; its shard matrix row reads skipped), Live E2E UI, Test UI. 18 completed skipped (UI lint, type check and build, docs build, opt-in harnesses, queue verdicts). STILL IN PROGRESS, no conclusion: Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 and Type Check · workspace (Type Check · consumer gates was still running at 15:53Z and had left the in-progress list by 15:55Z). No check-run failed. The test and build verdicts for this head are therefore not read by this record; nothing below rests on them, and the landing check (every check green) is not met yet.

### ① Derived judgments

1. In-process `getMetaItemLayered({ type, name })`, no `packageId`, a type the registry reads by package, a name two or more served packages register: resolved the first registered holder, now throws `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, 409). Accept set narrowed. RIGHT. The added call is `registry.resolveItem(type, name, null, member)` under `!request.packageId && readsByPackage(type) === true`, the same call under the same condition as the plain read's `packagelessScopedRead` (protocol-meta-item-reads.ts:594), after the same canonicalisation and member resolution. One producer (`readPackageScopedItem` over `resolvePackageScopedName`), so the layered read can refuse nothing the plain read does not already refuse at that address.
2. REST `GET /meta/:type/:name/layers` and `?layers=true`, host with no `objectQLProvider`: 200 with one holder's layers, now 409. Narrowed. RIGHT, a consequence of 1: the door calls `getMetaItemLayered` before its gate chain (rest-server.ts `serveMetaItemLayered`).
3. REST `/layers` catch now passes `packageScopedCandidates: true`: the 409 body gains `details.candidates`. Widened by one optional member on an existing refusal. RIGHT. Same `handleRouteError` option the plain read's catch passes (meta-item-read-routes.ts:1224), same recogniser (`packageScopedRefusalCandidates` in `@objectstack/types`, by shape).
4. Step 1c's refusal (`packagelessLayeredReadRefusal`, the package-less writes' sentence) gains `refusal: { status: 'refused', reason: 'ambiguous-in-environment', candidates }`. Sentence, code and status unchanged; both transports now answer `details.candidates`. Widened. RIGHT. The candidates are `packagelessAddress().candidates`, already sorted there (`[...bindings].sort()`), and are the holders the sentence names. The save and delete doors call `packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal` directly and do not pass through `withPackageCandidates`, so their answer does not move; pinned (`saveRefusal.refusal` undefined, and no `details` on the writes on both transports).
5. Side effect of 4, read and found harmless: that error now satisfies the by-shape `isPackageScopedRefusal` readers (runtime meta.ts, plugin-security). It is produced only by the door chain's step 1c and thrown to the layered route's catch, never from `getMetaItemLayered`, so no in-process reader meets it.
6. `protocol.ts`: docblock only. No accept set moves.
7. Not declared, and it moves (finding F1 in ④): REST `GET /meta/:type/:name/published`, bare, on the same no-engine host.

The 409 shape against the plain read's, for the two declared moves: identical. Same thrown object class from the same resolver call, so the same `code` (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT`), `status` (409), message, and `refusal.candidates` in the same order and content; on REST both catches hand it to `handleRouteError` with the same option, so the body is `{ error, code, details: { candidates } }` on both. On the dispatcher the layered route answers through `errorFromThrown` and the plain read through `packageScopedRefusalAnswer`; that pair predates this diff (#32250) and is pinned in meta-qualified-item-read.test.ts. The new REST pins compare candidates sorted, not in order; the order equality holds by construction, not by pin.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/32622-layers-two-holders-candidates.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch, `@objectstack/rest` patch. Matches what the diff publishes: source moves in those two packages only; `packages/runtime` carries tests alone.
- Level: patch is the level AGENTS.md step 3 sets for `Metadata-protocol: none` ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"). RIGHT.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: RIGHT. No key, accepted value or metadata type an author writes changes; the moved answers are reads.
- `!` in the title and in the changeset summary line; `**BREAKING**` banner with FROM, TO and the one-line fix ("name the package"). Present.
- ADR-0087: exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The gate refuses that category only on a declared `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (#32601); this changeset declares `none` with the `(narrowing)` arm, so it is admissible, and the check-runs that carry `check:adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` read success on this head.
- Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body.
- Defect: the banner says "Two answers move". Three do on the tree (F1). The FROM and TO of the third are not in the changeset or the PR body.

Clause-②: no (narrowing). The arm is the right one: nothing a published schema accepts changes, and two declared answers plus one undeclared go from served to refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation "Clause-② kept as the claim's `no`": answered by the rework (addendum 6897100983): PR body and changeset now carry `no (narrowing)`, the bang and the banner. The claim comments on #32622 and #32914 still read `Clause-②: no`; no gate reads them. Accepted as recorded.
- Dev `open_questions` (protocol.ts docblocks under-describe two answers): half answered at this head. The `packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` docblock now carries both sentences. The `getMetaItemLayered` method docblock ("its contract") still has no `@throws` for the two-holder refusal (nit N2).
- File surface: the #32622 claim says "no `protocol.ts` (stop on breach; explain in the report)". The head edits `protocol.ts` (docblock, +7/-2), explained in the addendum by a "seat rule change 14:45Z" that is not among the cards or the PR I read. ESCALATED to the seat: confirm that rule change covers this edit. The diff there is comment-only on the tree.
- `Skills-docs:` line: a `(narrowing)` arm owes the PR body a third declaration line (pm-dispatch SKILL.md, the `Metadata-protocol:` template; review-checklist: missing means REWORK). The PR body has none. ESCALATED to the lane seat; a PR-body edit, no head move.
- Dogfood battery: owed by the `!` and the arm; reported on `fa7fb66a7c` (467 files, 3959 tests), one commit below the head. The head commit above it is `e516f353`, whose diff I read as comment-only in `protocol.ts`. The seat's pre-queue check owns pinning it to the head.
- Other deviations in the report (commit trailers, repo-wide lint left to CI, draft PR opened late, lock hold times, pre-merge reds on unbuilt packages): process, no contract effect; the lane seat's.
- Always-check (SQL pushdown): no new id materialisation or in-app join. The added judgment is one in-memory registry call.

### ④ Design judgment

Does the narrowing take a declared capability away, or make the spec's own refusal real? It makes the refusal real.

- ADR-0150 D3 on `main`: "A caller with no package ... resolves against the whole environment: the environment item of that name first ..., else the unique package holder, else the refusal with candidates (`409` at a door, D5)." Nothing in D3, D5 or the published `GetMetaItemLayeredRequestSchema` declares "the first registered holder" as an answer; the schema's `packageId` text describes the collision as something the package id resolves. The first-holder answer was the artifact lookup's fallback, an implementation gap, and the plain read at the same address already refused it. #32914's constraint ("never answer a bare name by picking one holder", "No relaxation") is met.
- The remedy stays served: `packageId` / `?package=` reads each holder's layers (pinned in every composition), and a name one package holds is unchanged (CONTROL pin).
- Tried to break it. (a) A registry with `readsByPackage` and no `resolveItem`: refused earlier by `refuseUnjudgeableByNameRead`, so the new call cannot hit a missing method. (b) One enabled and one disabled registered holder: `servedAddressJudgment` re-addresses the read to the served holder before the new guard, so `packageId` is set and the resolver is not asked; the read is served as before. (c) Stored-row holders beside a disabled package (the #32354 Q2 state): the judgment leaves `packageId` unset and the resolver is asked of the registry only; the dev reports the Q2 in-process pin green, and on this head that rests on Test Core, which has not concluded. (d) An app read by its package-id key: the resolver finds no holder of that name and returns, no new refusal. (e) Draft layer (`withDraft`): judged before any layer, as the plain read judges before its draft switch.

Every caller of `getMetaItemLayered` in the tree at this head (grep over the whole repo; `ui/**` holds no in-process caller, only HTTP readers of `/layers`, whose default-host answer was already 409):

| caller | meets the new throw? | handled |
|---|---|---|
| plugin-security `packaged-permission-set-lock-gate.ts:96` | yes (`permission` is read by package) | yes: `refusedPackageHolders` reads `refusal.candidates` and reads each holder at its package; the lock now judges every holder, not the first |
| plugin-security `security-catalog-echo.ts` `echoRowAt` via `echoSecurityCatalogMutation` | yes, for `permission` (`position` is not read by package) | yes when the event names no package; see N1 for the package-unbound address |
| plugin-security `echoRowIsServed` | yes, for an unowned `permission` slot | yes: the throw reaches `dropGoneEchoSlots`' catch, the slot is kept ("unread is not gone") |
| rest `rest-server.ts:3871` `fetchCurrentMetaDocument` | no: `getMetaItem` is asked first and already refuses | n/a |
| rest `rest-server.ts:4449` `/layers`, `?layers=true` | yes | yes: the route catch, with candidates (this diff) |
| rest `meta-item-history-routes.ts:1371` `/published` | yes, when no engine is wired (the plain read is asked first only behind the engine's registry) | rethrown as 409 by the `overlayError.status` rule, to a catch that carries no candidates: F1 |
| runtime `meta.ts:1005` `answerMetaLayered` (`/layers`, `?layers=`) | yes | yes: `errorFromThrown`, with candidates |
| runtime `meta.ts:1636` `/published` | yes, when the engine's registry is not reachable | swallowed (only `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` is answered), falls through to the snapshot: F1 |

Findings:

- **F1, should-fix. A third REST answer moves and is not declared; its dispatcher twin does not move.** `GET /meta/:type/:name/published`, naming no package, a name two served packages register, on a REST host with no `objectQLProvider` (the composition the PR's own table calls "no engine wired"). Read on the tree, not measured: the route asks the plain read first only when the engine's registry answers `isPackageDisabled` (meta-item-history-routes.ts:1337-1349); without it, it calls `getMetaItemLayered({ type, name })` and rethrows any error carrying a numeric `status` (:1404-1424). Before this diff that call returned, and the route went on to its overlay or snapshot exit; now it throws 409, which the route's final catch answers through `handleRouteError(res, error)` with no `details.candidates`. That is the right direction (the engine-wired `/published` already answers the plain read's 409), and it is the spec's own refusal, so it is not a must-fix. But the changeset banner and the PR body's `Clause-②` line both say two answers move and name `/layers` and the in-process read only; a breaking changeset owes each FROM and TO (AGENTS.md step 3). The dispatcher's `/published` in the matching composition catches the same throw and serves the snapshot (runtime meta.ts:1632-1670), so the two transports now differ there, and neither answer is pinned. Fix on the prose faces alone, which keeps this record governing: add the `/published` FROM and TO to the changeset banner and the PR body (or state there that it was measured not to move). File a follow-up card for the rest: pin both transports' bare `/published` in the no-engine composition, give the REST answer its `details.candidates`, and decide the dispatcher twin's swallow. Delta review owed on the wording.
- **N1, nit.** `echoSecurityCatalogMutation` recovers from the refusal only when the event's address is `undefined`. For a `permission` event at the package-unbound address (`packageId: null`) of a name two packages register in code, `echoRowAt` now throws where it used to read the layers and then skip (the registry serves the name). Reachable through a legacy package-unbound row at boot, where the loop catches and logs a warning that the echo "failed"; a mutation projector is best-effort and warns. No grant, lock or served answer changes. Follow-up card or accepted deviation.
- **N2, nit.** The `getMetaItemLayered` method docblock in `protocol.ts`, which the body file calls its contract, lists no `@throws` for the two-holder `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (nor for the 501 and exact-qualifier refusals that predate this diff). The new throw is described in the neighbouring `packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` docblock only. A comment-only edit to a code file moves the head, so: follow-up card.
- **N3, nit.** The new REST pins compare `details.candidates` sorted, so they would not catch an order difference from the plain read. The order is equal by construction (one resolver call). Accepted.

No must-fix. One should-fix (F1), closable on the prose faces plus a follow-up card.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `e516f3534bd5f0d4eb74c140f8da53b2d4ec31ff`
Area: S4 / E1 · Fixes #32622 #32914
Contract-review record: https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/33885#issuecomment-6897231104 (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, narrowing face, isolated run). Its verdict is PASS, with no must-fix and one should-fix. A delta review of that fix is owed before landing.

1. **The narrowing.** It makes the ADR-0150 D3/D5 refusal real on the layered read, and takes no declared capability away.
   - The added `registry.resolveItem(type, name, null, member)` call runs under the same condition as the plain read's `packagelessScopedRead`.
   - The 409 has the plain read's error class, code, status and `details.candidates`.
   - `packageId` and `?package=` still serve each holder.
2. **F1 · should-fix · a third answer moves and is not declared.** Bare `GET /meta/:type/:name/published` on a REST host with no `objectQLProvider` reaches `getMetaItemLayered` without asking the plain read first. It rethrows any error that carries a numeric status: I spot-checked `meta-item-history-routes.ts` around lines 1400–1424 on the head.
   - So that route now answers 409, with no `details.candidates`.
   - The dispatcher twin (`runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`) swallows the same throw and serves the snapshot, so the two transports now differ, and neither is pinned.
   - Fix on the prose faces:
     - Add the `/published` FROM → TO to the changeset banner and to the PR body's `Clause-②` line.
     - File a follow-up card for three things: the pins, the candidates on that 409, and the dispatcher swallow.
   - The delta review reads only that prose move.
3. **Nits.** These are follow-up material; none of them moves the head.
   - N1: `echoSecurityCatalogMutation` recovers only on an `undefined` address. A package-unbound `permission` event on a two-holder name now throws where it used to skip. It produces a warning only.
   - N2: the `getMetaItemLayered` docblock has no `@throws` for the new refusal.
   - N3: the REST pins compare candidates sorted, so order equality holds by construction.
4. **PR-body items for the area to fix with F1.**
   - The PR body has no `Skills-docs:` line, which a `(narrowing)` arm owes.
   - The claim comments still read `Clause-②: no`. No gate reads them.
5. **Seat's call.** The #32622 claim says "no `protocol.ts`", but the head edits the `protocol.ts` docblock under a "seat rule change 14:45Z" that is not on the card. The edit is comment-only, but the seat should confirm the rule.
6. **Semver and declaration.**
   - The changeset is `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/rest`, with `Metadata-protocol: none`.
   - It has the `!`, the BREAKING banner, and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
   - All of this matches the repo rules for a non-protocol narrowing.
   - The dogfood battery (467 passed, 3 skipped) was run at `fa7fb66a7c`, one comment-only commit below the head.
7. **File surface.** 10 files, all of them the protocol, REST and runtime files of this change plus their tests.
8. **Check-runs on the head at review time:** 26 success, 18 skipped, and 9 still in progress (Build Core, Test Core 1–8 of 8, Type Check · workspace). None has failed. Arm only once all are green.

## Review — FAIL (amended, ACCEPT read per review-checklist.md)

Head-sha: `e516f3534bd5f0d4eb74c140f8da53b2d4ec31ff`
This amends verdict 6897239914 on the same head. The contract-review record 6897231104 (PASS, with should-fix F1) is unchanged. Read against review-checklist.md, the ordinary review is REWORK on these items:

1. **REWORK: the PR body has no `Skills-docs:` line.** A `(narrowing)` arm owes it, and review-checklist.md says a missing line is REWORK. This is a PR-body edit.
2. **F1 (should-fix, from the record).** Declare the third moved answer: bare `GET /meta/:type/:name/published` on a REST host with no engine now answers 409 with no candidates. Add its FROM → TO to the changeset banner and to the `Clause-②` line, and file the follow-up card (pins, candidates, dispatcher swallow).
